cross_references.label: Lab. Code §3700.5
cross_references.description: Criminal penalties for §3700 violation. Knowing failure to secure = misdemeanor ($10K fine / 1 yr jail); second offense or > 50 employees = felony. §3700 obligation + §3700.5 criminal exposure operate as a pair — one defines the duty, the other enforces it.

cross_references.label: Lab. Code §3702
cross_references.description: Certificate of Consent to Self-Insure requirements. §3700(b) option (individual self-insurance) is only available with a §3702 certificate from DWC Director. Certificate is the proof of §3700(b) compliance.

cross_references.label: Lab. Code §3706
cross_references.description: Uninsured employer loses assumption of risk, contributory negligence, and fellow-servant defenses. Negligence presumed. This is the tort-track enabler when §3700 fails — the worker can sue in civil court for full damages including pain and suffering.

cross_references.label: Lab. Code §§3715-3717 (UEBTF)
cross_references.description: Uninsured Employers Benefit Trust Fund. When §3700 fails, UEBTF pays worker's WC benefits and pursues the employer for recovery. Three-track strategy (WCAB/UEBTF + tort + criminal referral) opens when §3700 is violated.

cross_references.label: Lab. Code §3601
cross_references.description: §3601 grants tort immunity to compliant employers. §3700 is the precondition: the exclusive remedy bargain only works if coverage is secured. Uninsured employer cannot invoke §3601 immunity. §3700 and §3601 are two sides of the same bargain.

cross_references.label: Lab. Code §3202 (liberal construction)
cross_references.description: §3202 liberal construction applies when coverage disputes arise under §3700. Exclusions from coverage construed narrowly. Employer label challenges (misclassification) resolved in favor of worker where evidence is ambiguous. See Western Growers v. WCAB (1993).

cross_references.label: Lab. Code §4553 (serious and willful misconduct enhancement)
cross_references.description: Where employer deliberately fails to secure coverage (§3700 violation) and the non-coverage is itself serious and willful misconduct, §4553's 50% compensation enhancement applies to the underlying WC award. Deliberate misclassification as an independent contractor to avoid §3700 coverage can constitute §4553 conduct.

cross_references.label: Lab. Code §132a (discrimination for filing WC claim)
cross_references.description: Misclassification post-injury to deny WC coverage can constitute §132a discrimination. Worker who is reclassified as 'independent contractor' after filing or threatening to file a WC claim has a §132a retaliation claim.

cross_references.label: Lab. Code §226 (wage statement requirements)
cross_references.description: Wage statements showing worker as 1099 vs. W-2 employee are evidence in §3700 coverage disputes. Missing or altered payroll records in misclassification cases implicate both §3700 and §226.
